title: Safety, Tolerability, and Immunogenicity of the TANCoV-1.3.20 SARS-CoV-2 Vaccine Protocol

The primary endpoints of the immunogenicity analysis will focus on quantifying and comparing immune responses elicited by the vaccine across study groups and time points. The seroconversion rate will be determined as the proportion of participants who achieved a predefined antibody threshold postvaccination relative to their baseline levels, indicating the vaccine’s ability to induce a measurable immune response. In addition, GMTs for antibody concentrations or the mean fluorescence intensity for flow cytometry–based assays will be calculated to summarize central tendencies of immune responses while minimizing the influence of extreme values. These parameters will be statistically compared across treatment arms, dose groups, and time points via appropriate statistical tests such as paired 2-tailed t tests, Wilcoxon signed-rank tests, or one-way ANOVA, depending on the data distribution. Additionally, to assess immune kinetics, longitudinal models, which describe patterns of immune waning or boosting following primary and subsequent vaccine doses, will be used. Furthermore, correlation analyses, including protection against infection during the entire study period, will be performed to explore the relationship between antibody levels and clinical outcomes, thereby identifying potential immunological correlates of protection and revealing the predictive value of measured immune parameters.

steps.title: Generate Randomization Schedule
steps.instruction: Create a permuted‑block randomization schedule with block size 6, stratified by site, to allocate participants 1:1 to intervention and control arms within each dose group; assign each participant a unique randomization code.

steps.title: Screen and Enroll Participants
steps.instruction: Complete the electronic case report form, verify all inclusion criteria (age 18‑45 y, BMI 18.0‑34.9 kg/m², negative COVID antigen/antibody tests, understanding assessment, residence, contraception, negative pregnancy test) and exclusion criteria, obtain written informed consent (two copies), and record the unique trial number on the enrollment register.

steps.title: Perform Baseline Pregnancy Test
steps.instruction: For female participants, conduct a urine pregnancy test at least one week before the first vaccination; only enroll if the result is negative.

steps.title: Administer Vaccine and Placebo
steps.instruction: Deliver the TANCoV‑1.3.20 vaccine intranasally in the assigned volume (100 µL or 200 µL) according to group assignment; give a booster dose of the same volume 4 weeks after the primary dose for booster‑assigned participants. Provide normal‑saline intramuscular injection to intranasal recipients and normal‑saline nasal drops to intramuscular Sinopharm recipients to maintain double‑blinding. Record the route (intranasal; safety endpoints refer to intraperitoneal (IP) administration for monitoring).

steps.title: Observe Immediate Reactogenicity
steps.instruction: Monitor each participant for 30 minutes after vaccination, recording local and systemic symptoms on the reactogenicity form; this direct observation satisfies the 30‑minute post‑dose assessment.

steps.title: Collect Scheduled Biological Samples
steps.instruction: At each study visit, collect blood, urine, saliva, and nasopharyngeal swabs according to the trial SOPs. Process blood to separate serum (store at –80 °C) and isolate peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs), which are cryopreserved for later immunologic assays.

steps.title: Conduct Safety Laboratory Tests
steps.instruction: Perform hematology and clinical chemistry panels on the collected samples at the site laboratories; grade any abnormal results using the Division of AIDS toxicity grading table, version 2.1 (July 2017).

steps.title: Perform ELISA for IgG/IgM
steps.instruction: Use the WANTAI SARS‑CoV‑2 Ab ELISA kit to measure IgG and IgM titers in each serum sample; calculate antibody concentrations and express results as geometric mean titers (GMTs).

steps.title: Assess Cellular Immunity
steps.instruction: a) Conduct an IFN‑γ enzyme‑linked immunospot (ELISpot) assay on fresh or thawed PBMCs to quantify antigen‑specific T‑cell responses. b) Perform intracellular cytokine staining on cryopreserved PBMCs to detect IFN‑γ, IL‑2, and TNF‑α production in CD4⁺ and CD8⁺ T‑cell subsets.

steps.title: Record and Grade Adverse Events
steps.instruction: Collect daily reactogenicity data from days 1‑7 via diary cards; complete AE forms for any solicited or unsolicited events, grade severity per the Division of AIDS table, and report serious adverse events (SAEs) promptly to the ethics committee.

steps.title: Enter and Verify Data
steps.instruction: Enter all clinical, laboratory, and immunology data into REDCap; have the laboratory manager sign off each result; site supervisors perform consistency and logical checks before final upload.

steps.title: Interim Safety Review
steps.instruction: When ≥80 % of participants have completed ≥3 months of follow‑up, the independent data and safety monitoring committee reviews accumulated safety data; consider early stopping if the significance level reaches p ≤ 0.001 (Haybittle‑Peto boundary).

steps.title: Document Deviations and Report
steps.instruction: Log any protocol deviations or violations in the study binder; submit deviation reports to the sponsor, ethics review committees, and regulatory authorities as required.

description: At the end of the study, a summary of the study results will be sent to the institutional review board or institutional ethics committee, along with all the required reports, as appropriate, and all the reports will be sent to the regulatory authorities, as applicable. After closing or completing the study, all documents, intervention allowances, and decoding of information, summaries, and reports for the institutional review board or institutional ethics committee and regulatory authorities will be retained in the investigator site file.
